mainTopic: Whether מה לי לשקר works against a חזקה, how much a neighbor pays for a wall he uses, and how far rights gained in a neighbor's wall or courtyard reach.
overview: The גמרא asks whether a borrower who says 'I paid you before the due date' is believed. He could have said 'I paid on time' (מה לי לשקר), but people normally do not pay early (a חזקה). It tries to prove the answer from two lines in our משנה about neighbors who build a wall, and from another משנה about a borrowed מנה. All three proofs are pushed off, so the question is not decided here. Next the גמרא discusses a neighbor who leans a new wall on the high wall. רב הונא says leaning on half means paying for all of it, while רב נחמן says he pays only for what he used, and each admits one exception. רב הונא then rules that openings in the wall do not prove the neighbor paid his share. רב נחמן and רב יוסף argue about how far a right gained through use reaches, first with thin and thick beams, then with dripping and pouring rainwater. Each argument is reported in two versions, and רב יוסף actually ruled about a willow-branch hut. The amud ends as רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, begins a new teaching about someone who rents out a room.

steps.title: Does a presumption cancel the 'Why would I lie?' argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question. Maybe when the claim goes against a חזקה, we do not apply מה לי לשקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe, when there is a presumption against his claim, we do not say 'Why would I lie?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of a question it started just before this. Now it will look for proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The background is the rule that a person does not pay before the due date (אין אדם פורע תוך זמנו). If the borrower claims 'I paid early,' his claim goes against that חזקה. But he could have said 'I paid on time' and been believed. So which is stronger: the חזקה, or the מה לי לשקר?

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This opens the other side of a question.
A presumption, an assumption about how people normally act
Why would I lie? He is believed because he could have made a better claim.

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
where there is a presumption,
phrases.notes: The presumption is that people don't pay before the due date, so 'I paid early' sounds unlikely.

phrases.english: we do not say 'Why would I lie?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a two-sided question that began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a חזקה against the claim override the מה לי לשקר argument?

steps.title: Proof from the shared wall in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a neighbor is presumed to have paid his share of the wall unless the builder proves he didn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: He is presumed to have given, unless the other brings proof that he did not give.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה as a possible proof. In the next step it will work out how this line answers the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, two neighbors must build a wall together. Later one says, 'You never paid your share.' The משנה says the other neighbor is believed that he paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a proof.
Presumed to be
Proof, evidence

phrases.english: Come and hear:
He is presumed to have given,
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה, about two neighbors who built a dividing wall together.

phrases.english: unless he brings proof that he did not give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether מה לי לשקר applies against a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the shared wall: the neighbor is presumed to have paid.

steps.title: The משנה must mean he claimed he paid early
steps.stepSummary: Believing someone who says 'I paid on time' is obvious. So the משנה must be about 'I paid early,' and he is still believed. That means מה לי לשקר works even against a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he demanded payment after the due date and the other said 'I paid you on time,' that's obvious! So it must be that he said 'I paid you before the due date.' This shows that even against a presumption, we say 'Why would I lie?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the משנה is talking about. It concludes that the משנה supports using מה לי לשקר even against a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the claim were 'I paid on time,' the משנה would be teaching nothing new. So it must be about a claim of early payment, which goes against the חזקה. He is still believed, because he could have said 'I paid on time.'

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
If you say
It's obvious! That needs no teaching.
Rather, is it not that...
So we see, apparently
Within my time, before the due date

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say he demanded it after the due date,
and he said to him: 'I paid you at my due date,'
that's obvious!
Rather, is it not that he said to him:
'I paid you before my due date'?
Apparently, even where there is a presumption,
we say 'Why would I lie?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out what case the quoted משנה is about and draws the proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: מה לי לשקר works even against a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה believes him, and the case must be a claim of early payment.

steps.title: With a wall, each row is its own due date
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Payment for a wall comes due row by row, so 'early' payment is really payment on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because each and every row of the wall is its own due date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the shared wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a wall, every finished row of stones makes another payment due. So a neighbor who paid while the wall was still going up really paid on time. There is no חזקה against him here, and the case says nothing about our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
A row or layer of stones in a wall
Its time, its due date

phrases.english: Here it is different,
because each and every row is its own due date.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first case in the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is not truly 'before the due date,' because each row makes payment due.

steps.title: Proof from the wall above four אמות
steps.stepSummary: A second proof from the משנה: a neighbor is not obligated for wall height above four אמות. If he later builds another wall next to it, he must pay, and he is not believed that he paid unless he brings proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: For the part above four cubits, they do not obligate him. If he built another wall next to it, etc., [he must pay], unless he brings proof that he gave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second line from the משנה as a new proof. In the next step it will explain what case this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the משנה does NOT believe the neighbor's claim that he paid. That is the opposite result from step 2, so it may point the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the standard height of the shared wall
They do not obligate
Built next to, leaned against
A wall

phrases.english: Come and hear:
From four cubits and up,
they do not obligate him.
If he built another wall next to it, etc.,
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' skips the rest of the משנה: he then has to pay for the whole height.

phrases.english: unless he brings proof that he gave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, brings a new source from later in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether מה לי לשקר applies against a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the wall above four אמות: he is not presumed to have paid.

steps.title: Here he is not believed, so the presumption wins
steps.stepSummary: Someone who says 'I paid on time' should be believed. So the משנה must be about 'I paid early,' and he is not believed. That means מה לי לשקר does not work against a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he demanded payment after the due date and the other said 'I paid you on time,' why wouldn't he be believed? So it must be that he said 'I paid you before the due date.' This shows that against a presumption, we do not say 'Why would I lie?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same method as before. This time the משנה seems to prove the opposite: the חזקה beats מה לי לשקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A claim of 'I paid on time' should be believed, so it can't be the case where he loses. The case must be a claim of early payment. He is not believed even though he could have claimed 'I paid on time,' so the חזקה wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not?
He demanded it from him

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say he demanded it after its due date,
and he said to him: 'I paid you at my due date,'
why would he not be believed?
Rather, is it not that he said: 'I paid you before my due date'?
Apparently, where there is a presumption,
we do not say 'Why would I lie?'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא שֶׁתְּבָעוֹ לְאַחַר זְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the case in the second משנה and draws the opposite conclusion from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: מה לי לשקר does not work against a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה does not believe him, and the case must be a claim of early payment.

steps.title: He never expected to owe at all
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Here the neighbor would surely not pay early, because he didn't even think the רבנן would make him pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because he says: Who says the רבנן will obligate me to pay?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second proof as well. Neither proof settles the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor did not think he owed anything for the height above four אמות. So the idea that he paid early is especially hard to believe. That makes this case special, and it doesn't teach about an ordinary loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Who says? Who can be sure?
They will obligate
The רבנן, the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs from the wall משנה are rejected. The first case has a due date for every row, and the second has a neighbor who never expected to owe. So it is still open whether a חזקה beats מה לי לשקר.

phrases.english: Here it is different, because he says:
Who says the Rabbis will obligate me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the 'above four אמות' case in the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חזקה here is extra strong, since he didn't expect to owe at all. So it can't teach about ordinary early payment.

steps.title: A third proof begins: the case of the borrowed מנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא quotes a משנה. If a borrower who admitted the loan later says 'I gave it to you,' he is exempt. If he says 'You have nothing with me,' he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: Come and hear. Someone said, 'I have a מנה in your hand,' and the other said, 'Yes.' The next day he said, 'Give it to me.' If the borrower says, 'I gave it to you,' he is exempt. If he says, 'You have nothing with me,' he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof by quoting a משנה. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two answers the borrower can give the next day. 'I already gave it to you' gets him off, but 'You have nothing with me' makes him pay. The גמרא will try to explain why these two answers end up so differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: a source is about to be brought as a proof
A sum of money (one hundred זוז)
Yes
Exempt, does not have to pay
Liable, has to pay

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear:
'I have a maneh in your hand,'
phrases.notes: He means: you are holding a hundred of my money, because I lent it to you.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'Yes.'
The next day he said to him: 'Give it to me.'
If he said: 'I gave it to you,' he is exempt.
If he said: 'You have nothing in my hand,' he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second proof was rejected in step 7, a new source is brought on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether מה לי לשקר works against a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a borrower who admitted a loan of a מנה

steps.title: The proof: paying early is not believed even with a better claim available
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'You have nothing with me' as 'I paid you before the due date.' Since he is liable even though he could have said 'I paid on time,' it follows that מה לי לשקר does not work against a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it true that 'I gave it to you' means 'I paid you on time,' and 'You have nothing with me' means 'I paid you before the due date'? And the משנה says he is liable. So we see that where there is a חזקה, we do not say מה לי לשקר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה in a way that turns it into a proof that מה לי לשקר loses to a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a חזקה that people do not pay before the due date. The borrower could have claimed 'I paid on time' and been believed, yet when he claims early payment he is still liable. So his better possible claim (מה לי לשקר) does not save him against the חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that: introduces a suggested reading of the source
On my due date
Before my due date (early)
Apparently, so we see

phrases.english: What, isn't it that 'I gave it to you'
means he said to him: 'I paid you at my due time';
and 'You have nothing in my hand'
means he said to him: 'I paid you within my time'?
phrases.notes: 'Within my time' means before the loan was due, which is early.

phrases.english: And it teaches: he is liable.
So we see that where there is a presumption,
we do not say 'Why would I lie?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: מה לי לשקר does not work against a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'liable' ruling for 'You have nothing with me,' read as a claim of early payment

steps.title: Rejected: 'You have nothing with me' means 'there never was a loan'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'You have nothing with me' as a total denial of the loan. Someone who denies a loan he admitted is treated as if he said 'I never paid.' So the משנה has nothing to do with paying early.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'You have nothing with me' means 'This never happened.' As the master said: anyone who says 'I didn't borrow' is like someone who says 'I didn't pay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof by giving 'You have nothing with me' a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower is not claiming he paid early. He is denying the loan completely, even though he admitted it the day before. Once he is caught denying a real loan, he is treated as someone who never paid, so he is liable. The case says nothing about מה לי לשקר or a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: These things never happened
As the master said: quotes an accepted rule
I did not borrow
I did not pay back

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'You have nothing with me' is just another way to say 'I paid.' Here it means 'there never was a loan.' That is why it ends so differently from 'I gave it to you.'
steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs have been pushed off: the two from our משנה about the wall, and רב אחא's proof from the משנה about the borrowed מנה. The question of whether מה לי לשקר works against a חזקה is not settled on this amud.

phrases.english: No; what does 'You have nothing in my hand' mean?
'These things never happened,'
phrases.notes: He is saying the loan never took place at all.

phrases.english: As the master said:
Anyone who says 'I did not borrow'
is like one who says 'I did not repay.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading used in step 9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'You have nothing with me' is a denial of the loan, not a claim of early payment

steps.title: Back to our משנה: leaning a new wall against the high wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in our משנה: if the neighbor built another wall next to the high wall, he must pay his share for all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he built another wall next to it, the court makes him pay for all of it, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new part of our משנה. It is quoting the line it is about to discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor did not have to pay for the wall above four אמות. Once he leans a new wall on it, he shows he wants to use it, so he must pay for the whole wall. The next steps ask what happens if his new wall touches only part of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Built next to, leaned against
Wall
We put it on him, make him pay

phrases.english: If he built another wall next to it,
we roll everything onto him, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Everything' means his share of the whole wall, including the part above four אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A neighbor who builds another wall next to the high wall must pay his share for all of it.

steps.title: רב הונא: leaning on half counts as leaning on all
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if the new wall reaches only half of the high wall, the neighbor still pays for the whole wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If he leaned on half, he leaned on all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his ruling about a new wall that covers only part of the high wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treats a partial use as full use. The neighbor can easily extend his wall later, so he already pays for the whole wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Half
All of it

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
If he leaned on half, he leaned on all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the משנה's 'everything' reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building next to part of the wall obligates payment for the whole wall.

steps.title: רב נחמן: he pays only for what he used
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees. The neighbor pays only for the part of the wall his new wall actually leans on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: What he leaned on, he leaned on. What he did not lean on, he did not lean on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן argues with רב הונא about the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן looks only at what the neighbor actually did now. The parts of the wall he has not used yet are not charged to him.

keyTerms.meaning: For the part he leaned on
He did not lean on it

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: partial use means paying for the whole wall. רב נחמן: pay only for the part used.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
For what he leaned on, he leaned on;
for what he did not lean on, he did not lean on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The neighbor pays only for the part of the wall he actually built next to.

steps.title: רב הונא admits: a corner-type attachment
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא agrees that in the case of קרנא ולופתא, a corner-type attachment, the neighbor does not pay for the whole wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא admits in the case of a corner and an attachment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב הונא's ruling by giving a case where even he agrees with רב נחמן's result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's reason is that the neighbor will probably extend his wall. With this kind of corner attachment that is unlikely, so even רב הונא does not charge him for the whole wall.

keyTerms.meaning: And he admits, agrees
A corner and an attachment: a structure built at the corner

phrases.english: And Rav Huna admits
in the case of a corner and an attachment.
phrases.notes: In this case even רב הונא agrees he pays only for what he used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב הונא's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a corner attachment, even רב הונא charges only for the part used.

steps.title: רב נחמן admits: a roof beam or carved beam holes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees that if the neighbor puts an אפריזא, a beam, on the wall or carves holes for beams, he pays for the whole wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן admits in the case of a beam laid on the wall, and holes cut for beams.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב נחמן's ruling by giving a case where even he agrees with רב הונא's result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laying a beam or cutting beam holes shows the neighbor plans to use the whole wall. So even רב נחמן makes him pay for all of it, even though he has not yet used every part.

keyTerms.meaning: A beam or ledge placed on the wall
Holes cut out for fixing
Beams

steps.whatToRemember: Each side has an exception. רב הונא lets a corner attachment pay only for the part used. רב נחמן charges for the whole wall when there is a beam or beam holes, which show a plan to use all of it.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman admits in the case of a beam,
and in the case of holes cut for beams.
phrases.notes: Holes carved into the wall to set roof beams in, a clear sign he plans to build on all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches step 14 by limiting רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A beam or beam holes obligate payment for the whole wall, even according to רב נחמן.

steps.title: Openings in the wall do not prove the neighbor paid
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that openings in the wall facing the neighbor do not create a חזקה that the neighbor paid his share, even if the builder made sills for them. The builder can say he made them ahead of time so his wall would not be damaged later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: Openings in the wall do not create a presumption that the neighbor paid, even if the builder made sills for them. The builder can say: I thought that when you finally pay me, I don't want my wall damaged by cutting new holes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא teaches that openings on the neighbor's side of the wall do not prove the neighbor paid for the wall. The builder still keeps his claim that he was never paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the builder made beam-openings facing the neighbor only because the neighbor was a paying partner. רב הונא says no. The builder has a good explanation: he planned ahead so that, once the neighbor paid, no one would need to cut new holes and weaken the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal presumption; here, a presumption that the neighbor paid
Openings or holes in the wall, suited for resting beams
Sills or ledges built for those openings
You will appease me, meaning pay me what you owe
My wall

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
openings in the wall do not create a presumption,
phrases.notes: He means a presumption that the neighbor paid his share of the wall, which is the question from the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דַּעֲבַד לֵיהּ הִימְלָטֵי.
phrases.english: and even if he made sills for them.
For the builder can say to him: I said to myself,
when you will appease me (and pay),
my wall should not be damaged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בֵּי כַוֵּי – לָא הָוֵי חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how much the neighbor pays to whether physical signs on the wall prove he already paid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Openings and sills facing the neighbor do not create a חזקה that he paid for the wall.

steps.title: Rights to thin beams versus thick beams
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that a right to place thin beams on a neighbor's wall does not include thick beams. A right to place thick beams does include thin beams.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says: If he gained the right to thin beams, he has not gained the right to thick beams. If he gained the right to thick beams, he has gained the right to thin beams.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן discusses someone who used his neighbor's wall for beams without protest and so gained a right to do it. He rules on how far that right reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick beams put a heavier load on the wall than thin ones. So allowing the lighter use does not mean allowing the heavier use. Allowing the heavier use does cover the lighter one.

keyTerms.meaning: He gained a right by using something without the owner protesting
Thin beams
Thick beams

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says:
If he gained the right to thin beams, he has not gained the right to thick beams,
phrases.notes: This means beams resting on the neighbor's wall, with the neighbor never protesting.

phrases.english: but if he gained the right to thick beams, he has gained the right to thin beams.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַחְזֵיק לְהוּרְדֵי – לָא אַחְזֵיק לִכְשׁוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about rights in a neighbor's wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A right to thin beams does not extend to thick beams. A right to thick beams includes thin beams.

steps.title: רב יוסף: thin beams include thick beams
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees with רב נחמן and rules that a right to thin beams also gives the right to thick beams.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says: If he gained the right to thin beams, he has gained the right to thick beams.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף argues with רב נחמן's first half. In his view, a right to thin beams covers thick beams too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two argue only about the thin-to-thick direction. Both agree that a right to thick beams covers thin ones. רב יוסף goes further and treats the right as reaching thick beams too.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef says:
If he gained the right to thin beams, he has gained the right to thick beams.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אַחְזֵיק לְהוּרְדֵי – אַחְזֵיק לִכְשׁוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן's ruling about thin beams.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A right to thin beams includes thick beams.

steps.title: Another version of רב נחמן agrees with רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: According to another version, רב נחמן also holds that either right includes the other. A right to thin beams covers thick beams, and a right to thick beams covers thin beams.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב נחמן says: If he gained the right to thin beams, he has gained the right to thick beams. If he gained the right to thick beams, he has gained the right to thin beams.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רב נחמן said. In this report he holds the same as רב יוסף, so there is no argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב נחמן limited the thin-beam right. In this version, he says the right goes both ways. This matches רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say; it introduces a second version of a statement

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Nachman says:
If he gained the right to thin beams, he has gained the right to thick beams,
and if he gained the right to thick beams, he has gained the right to thin beams.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב נחמן's view from step 17, which now matches רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, a right to either kind of beam includes the other kind.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same רב נחמן reported a second way. In this version he agrees with רב יוסף.

steps.title: Rights to dripping water versus pouring water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that a right to let rainwater drip off the roof into a neighbor's courtyard includes pouring it through a pipe. A right to pour does not include dripping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says: If he gained the right to dripping water, he has gained the right to pouring water. If he gained the right to pouring water, he has not gained the right to dripping water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a second, similar ruling, this time about rainwater running from one person's roof into a neighbor's courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dripping water falls along the whole edge of the roof. Pouring through a drainpipe sends it to one spot. A neighbor who put up with dripping all along the edge would accept water in one place. But accepting one stream does not mean accepting water along the whole edge.

keyTerms.meaning: Dripping water, falling along the edge of the roof
Pouring water, sent out through a drainpipe

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says:
If he gained the right to dripping water, he has gained the right to pouring water,
phrases.notes: He means water from his roof landing in the neighbor's courtyard.

phrases.english: but if he gained the right to pouring water, he has not gained the right to dripping water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַחְזֵיק לְנִטְפֵי – אַחְזֵיק לְשָׁפְכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling by רב נחמן on another kind of neighbor right, following the beam case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dripping right includes pouring. A pouring right does not include dripping.

steps.title: רב יוסף: even pouring includes dripping
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees and rules that even a right to pour through a pipe gives the right to let water drip from the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף says: Even if he gained the right to pouring water, he has gained the right to dripping water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף argues with the second half of רב נחמן's water ruling. He holds that a pouring right covers dripping too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a dripping right includes pouring. The word 'even' shows that רב יוסף goes further: a pouring right also includes dripping. So for him, either water right covers the other.
steps.whatToRemember: In both the beam case and the water case, רב יוסף holds that a right of use reaches the other related use too. In the first version of רב נחמן's view, the right covers only the use that is equal to it or lighter.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef says:
Even if he gained the right to pouring water, he has gained the right to dripping water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ אַחְזֵיק לְשָׁפְכֵי – אַחְזֵיק לְנִטְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן's limit on the pouring right.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A right to pour water through a pipe also includes letting it drip from the roof.

steps.title: Another version of רב נחמן: pouring and dripping include each other, but not a willow hut
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב נחמן says a right to pour includes dripping and a right to drip includes pouring. Neither right covers dripping from a hut roofed with willow branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב נחמן said: If a person gained the right to pour water through a pipe into his neighbor's courtyard, he also has the right to let it drip from his roof. If he gained the right to let it drip, he also has the right to pour. But he does not have the right to let water drip from a hut roofed with willow branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what רב נחמן held about rainwater rights. This version is broader than the one in Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רב נחמן said dripping includes pouring, but pouring does not include dripping. Here he says each right includes the other. He also adds a new limit: the right does not stretch to letting water drip from a hut roofed with willow branches.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say. It introduces a second version of a teaching.
He gained a חזקה, an established right through use.
Pouring water, a stream through a pipe.
Dripping water, drops falling from the roof edge.
A hut whose roof is made of willow branches.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 20. That was רב נחמן's first version, where pouring did NOT include dripping. In this version, both rights include each other.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Nachman said:
If he gained the right to pour, he gained the right to drip;
phrases.notes: Pouring means a stream of water through a drainpipe. Dripping means drops falling off the edge of the roof.

phrases.english: if he gained the right to drip, he gained the right to pour,
but to let water drip from a hut of willow branches, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב נחמן's ruling from Step 20. It is broader and adds a new limit about a willow hut.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A right to pour and a right to drip each include the other, but neither includes dripping from a willow-branch hut.

steps.title: רב יוסף: even dripping from a willow hut is included
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees with this version of רב נחמן. He holds the right covers even dripping from a willow-branch hut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Even a hut of willow branches is included.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף argues with the limit רב נחמן just set. He says the right reaches even to a hut roofed with willow branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן and רב יוסף agree that pouring and dripping include each other. Their argument is only about the willow hut. רב יוסף stretches the right further and includes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Even. It signals going one step further.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ צְרִיפָא דְאוּרְבָּנֵי.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Even a hut of willow branches.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ צְרִיפָא דְאוּרְבָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the willow-hut limit in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The right also covers dripping from a willow-branch hut.

steps.title: רב יוסף ruled this way in a real case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב יוסף actually decided a real case about a willow-branch hut, following his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף made an actual ruling about a hut of willow branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רב יוסף's view was not just theory. He used it to decide a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that a sage acted on his view (עבד עובדא) shows he held it firmly enough to rule in practice. Here, רב יוסף allowed dripping from a willow-branch hut.

keyTerms.meaning: He did an action. This means he gave a ruling in a real case.

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, everyone agrees that pouring and dripping include each other. The only argument is about a willow-branch hut. רב יוסף includes it, and he actually ruled that way.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef performed an action (made a real ruling)
regarding a hut of willow branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב יוסף acted on the view he stated in Step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף actually ruled that a right to let water fall into a courtyard includes dripping from a willow-branch hut.

steps.title: New teaching begins: someone who rents a room to another
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, starts a new teaching about a person who rents out a room. The ruling itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: If someone rents a room to another person...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and is setting up the next ruling. So far we only have the opening case, renting a room; the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh teaching, not part of the argument about rainwater. רב נחמן passes it on from his teacher רבה בר אבוה. The actual law about the renter comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rents out (to someone else).
A house or a room.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
One who rents a room to another

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: הַמַּשְׂכִּיר בַּיִת לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the rainwater discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: So far only the case is given: someone who rents a room to another. The ruling comes next.
